previous_description: Inline data type definition using a subset of JSON Schema Draft 7, used within API operations to describe request/response data shapes. For reusable canonical types, reference data-model layer entities instead. OpenAPI 3.0 restriction: a '$ref' within a Schema ignores all sibling keywords — unlike JSON Schema where $ref can be merged with other constraints.
definition: A data-shape definition, expressed as an OpenAPI 3.0 Schema Object, that constrains the type and structure of a value exchanged over the API, such as a request body, response body, parameter or header value. It is either a named entry under components/schemas or an inline schema nested in a media type, parameter, header or another schema.

distinguish_from.when: the element is the MIME-type-keyed content entry (e.g. application/json) that wraps a schema together with examples and encoding, rather than the shape definition itself
the element is a named operation input with a location (path, query, header or cookie), whose value type is merely described by a referenced schema
the element is the registry that holds reusable schemas, responses and parameters, not an individual type definition
the element is a concrete sample value illustrating data, rather than the constraints the data must satisfy

code_evidence: A DTO or model class used as a route's request or response type and annotated for OpenAPI generation, such as a Pydantic model passed as response_model in FastAPI, a NestJS class with @ApiProperty fields, or a Java class with @Schema.
An entry under '#/components/schemas/' or a 'schema:' block beneath 'content' in an openapi.yaml/json file, containing keywords such as type, properties, required, items, allOf or $ref.
A validation schema object attached to a route definition, such as a Fastify route 'schema: { body, response }', a zod/joi schema converted to OpenAPI, or a model class emitted by openapi-generator.

attribute_descriptions.name: type
attribute_descriptions.description: The JSON data type of the value: one of string, number, integer, boolean, array or object. OpenAPI 3.0 does not allow type arrays or 'null'. Set it on every non-$ref, non-composed schema.

attribute_descriptions.name: title
attribute_descriptions.description: A short human-readable label for the schema, typically the model or DTO name. Set it when documentation tooling should display a name other than the component key.

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Explanatory text for the schema or property, in CommonMark. Set it whenever the meaning of the value is not obvious from its name and type.

attribute_descriptions.name: format
attribute_descriptions.description: A modifier refining 'type', such as int32, int64, float, double, byte, binary, date, date-time, password, email or uuid. Set it when the base type alone does not convey the value's encoding or semantics.

attribute_descriptions.name: default
attribute_descriptions.description: The value the server assumes when the consumer omits this property or parameter. It must conform to the schema's type. Set it only when an actual server-side default exists.

attribute_descriptions.name: enum
attribute_descriptions.description: The closed list of literal values the data may take, each valid against the schema's type. Set it for fixed vocabularies such as status codes or modes.

attribute_descriptions.name: nullable
attribute_descriptions.description: Boolean, default false. When true, null is an accepted value in addition to the declared type (the OpenAPI 3.0 substitute for type: [T, null]). Set it when the API may send or accept explicit nulls.

notes: OpenAPI 3.0 uses an extended subset of JSON Schema Wright Draft 00, not Draft 7; correct this. The word 'inline' conflicts with components composing schemas. 'type' needs an enum. 'default' should be typed any and 'enum' typed array. Validation keywords are missing: minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, pattern, additionalProperties, not, minItems/maxItems. Boundary with data-model.jsonschema needs a rule.
